$comment: Every known zbc consumer. Hand-maintained: location + access + tier are facts no script can derive. access is `github` (clone repo), `local:<path>` (git archive off this machine) or `ssh:<host>:<path>` (git archive off another machine); `root` is where zbc.config.ts sits when it is not the repo root. The snapshot fields (mode, environments, instanceCount, ownModules, cliPin, vintage) are point-in-time as of snapshotDate. instanceCount is `.instance(` calls in non-test files under packages/infra/environments, so a factory counts once. ownModules is every directory under packages/infra/modules — copies of our own built-ins included; the survey, not this list, decides which are stale.

consumers.notes: Local-only git repo, no remote — cannot receive a GitHub PR. Heaviest consumer and the origin of the host-exec/vm/incus module family. ~30 sibling worktrees (foundry-*) plus forge-releases/ snapshots; review the canonical checkout only. forge-release is gone from its modules since 2026-09-02.

Still pins @zabaca/zbc 0.12.0 — now 11 minors behind (0.23.1). Clean subtree, no vendor drift. The `workspace` environment is a third env shape nothing else has. Worktrees cedarpad-{cmds,deploy,ping} on mac; the ryzen-9 checkout is stale (last commit 2026-08-24).

Largest copy-mode divergence: cloudflare is 734 diff-lines off upstream. The two checkouts have diverged — mac has `obs` and a `workstation` env, ryzen-9 has `lima-engine` and a `local` env and has not moved since 2026-08-15; GitHub matches mac, so treat ryzen-9 as abandoned. Sole author of posthog; gcp also in foothill-metabolic. Its vercel is a verbatim copy of zbc's own, which zbc deleted on 2026-07-10 (feee322).

Densest Cloudflare surface of any consumer, most of it token/zone/access plumbing. Authors two modules nothing upstream has (cloudflare-access-service-token, cloudflare-account-member). Worktree leeandco-seo on mac.

Only consumer besides zbc itself running the inbox app template (foothill-inbox, foothill-inbox-raw, foothill-inbox-auth-db). Its cloudflare copy is a 249-line fork of a 574-line upstream — an old ancestor, not a patch. Quiet since 2026-09-05 (1e391b9).
Two full clones on mac (web and zabaca-web) plus four zabaca-web-* worktrees; GitHub has pushes after both (2026-10-11), so survey from GitHub, never a local dir.

Moved from GitHub to agentgit.co (https://agentgit.co/agent-lab.git). Surveyed off the mac checkout because its agentgit credential helper is configured in that checkout only — pull it first. The Zabaca/agent-lab GitHub repo is a diverged leftover (last push 2026-08-26), not an ancestor of the live history. The live repo is a different consumer than the one surveyed on 2026-09-02: it dropped the ryzen-9 host-exec/vm environment for preview/production (r2 + its own stored-token). The ryzen-9 checkout is that old shape, stale since 2026-08-25 — so it is no longer the clean-subtree control case against foundry.

consumers.vintage: zbc-core-v0.10.2, copied by hand: no squash commit, no .zbc-vendor.json
consumers.notes: Local-only git repo, no remote. Its vendor/zbc is a hand copy, not a subtree — `git subtree add` could not reach zbc-core-v0.10.2 (its README.md:50-55) — so it has no update path. No environments or instances at all — pure module authoring. A per-client provisioning layer built on top of zbc; the strongest evidence for whatever composition primitive zbc is missing. Dormant: no commit since 2026-08-15. Not the same repo as varnick-app (Zabaca/varnick on GitHub).
Public repo. Smallest real consumer — good canary for whether an upgrade path works without inside knowledge.

Clean subtree, re-vendored since the last survey (was at cedarpad's d4cb29d, now be2b3f7). Grew from 1 instance to 5. Its scripts/release.mjs (post-deploy check, clean-tree refusal) was invisible to the collector until it learned .mjs on 2026-10-18. Worktrees games-{cars,nutmeg-online,online} on mac.
Public repo. Thinnest copy-mode consumer: one drifted module, one instance. Cheapest subtree-migration pilot. Dormant: no commit since 2026-07-30.

A client site (qualityom.com) — the closest thing to an outside company's shape. Copy mode vendored after subtree became the standard. Authors cloudflare-redirect-rules, which converges with railmid's cloudflare-redirect: two independent redirect modules, none upstream. Worktrees qom-{admin,confirm,form} on mac.

Wrote its own cloudflare-redirect module inside vendor/zbc/modules/ — a consumer file in the prefix, the case `zbc update --strict` refuses, and one a `subtree push` would deliver upstream. The survey sees it as a vendored module with no upstream history, i.e. novel. Worktree games-hidden-tab on mac is railmid's, despite the name.

Newest consumer and vendored at the current CLI, yet chose copy mode — worth asking why. Authors access-managed-oauth and secret-token; secret-token sits next to agent-lab's stored-token as a possible convergence.
Clean subtree. Three cloudflare-token instances beside one cloudflare and one cloudflare-access.
Public repo. Its stamp records CLI 0.21.1 over core v0.19.0 — a vintage mismatch at vendoring time. croft.zabaca.com is served from this repo's zabaca-zone instance.
Local-only git repo on mac, no remote. Clean subtree, cloudflare + cloudflare-token only.
Public repo; a Swift app whose zbc project lives in deploy/, not the repo root. Local dir name (launchy) matches neither id. A different repo from `varnick` on ryzen-9.

The only consumer outside the Zabaca org (artsmedia-dev/youbuzz), and zbc's origin: its CLI and module system (f1a4f99), turso and vercel were written on 2026-04-10/11, two weeks before zbc's first commit (42de911, 2026-04-24). Both match zbc revisions of 2026-04-29, so the survey calls them stale; zbc later deleted vercel (feee322, 2026-07-10); youbuzz's production environment still declares it as of its last readable commit. Its GitHub remote is not readable with our credentials, so it is surveyed off the local clone (last commit 2026-04-28), which may be behind.
zbc itself, live consumer of its own templates via symlink. Baseline for every drift measurement, never a PR target.
